Investigation shows that deleting `/tmp/*.so` and then `LD_BIND_NOW=1 opencode` fixes the issue, if it helps someone here 👍 

**It seems that opencode extract opentui lib in tmpfs and never clean up**. I didn't check yet, but seeing the number, it seems to be doing that for every subagent launched. At some point, tmpfs is full and opencode doesn't work anymore.
Forcing the linker to solve all references at starts seems to do the trick.

If you're running opencode in **tmux** on Linux, OOM kills are worse than you'd expect. The kernel doesn't just kill opencode. It killed my user `systemd`, which took tmux and my whole session with it.

I'm capping opencode with a systemd memory scope now. Alias in `.zshrc` / `.bashrc`:

```bash
# Memory-limit opencode so OOM kills don't take out your session
alias opencode="systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=8G -p MemorySwapMax=2G --description=opencode $HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode"
```

Set `MemoryMax` to whatever makes sense for your box (I'm on 16G, so 8G). The total ceiling is 10G (8G RAM + 2G swap). If opencode blows past the limit, the cgroup kills it and only it.

Note: if you run multiple opencode sessions, each gets its own 8G cap independently.

I agree, this makes it way too easy to inadvertently upload user data without informed consent. At the very least, there should be a confirmation dialog that informs the user what is being uploaded to where, and allows them to opt out.

This is a serious UX and privacy issue.
